name: 15-Minute Garlic Butter Shrimp Pasta
title: 15-Minute Garlic Butter Shrimp Pasta
description: Tender shrimp tossed with pasta in a garlic butter sauce, lemon and parsley.
instructions: Bring salted water to a boil and cook angel hair until just al dente; reserve 1/4 cup pasta water before draining.
Pat shrimp dry and season with listed salt and pepper so they sear instead of steam.
Melt half the butter in a wide skillet over medium-high; cook shrimp 1–2 minutes per side until pink and opaque, then transfer out.
Lower heat, add remaining butter, garlic and chilli flakes; stir 30–45 seconds until fragrant without browning garlic.
Add lemon juice, cooked pasta and a splash of pasta water; toss until butter forms a light sauce.
Return shrimp and parsley; check the thickest shrimp is opaque and reaches 63°C.
Taste for salt and pepper and serve immediately while glossy.

name: Idli
title: Idli
description: Idli, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Idli, rinse idli rice and urad dal separately; soak rice with poha and fenugreek, and dal in a second bowl for 4–6 hours.
Grind dal fluffy and rice slightly grainy, adding cold water in small amounts; mix with salt by hand.
Cover and ferment in a warm place 8–12 hours until risen and airy; the batter should smell pleasantly tangy, not sharply sour.
Stir gently, grease idli moulds and fill each cavity three-quarters full.
Steam above vigorously boiling water for 10–12 minutes; a toothpick through the centre should come out clean.
Rest moulds 2 minutes, loosen the edges with a wet spoon and unmould.
Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

name: Masala Dosa
title: Masala Dosa
description: Masala Dosa, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Masala Dosa, rinse dosa rice, urad dal and poha separately; soak with fenugreek 4–6 hours, then drain.
Grind dal fluffy and rice smooth with a little water; mix with salt and ferment covered 8–12 hours until bubbly and doubled.
Heat oil, crackle mustard, then cook onion, chilli, turmeric and curry leaves 2 minutes; add boiled potatoes and mash coarsely.
Heat a seasoned tawa to medium-high, wipe with oil and spread a ladle of batter in thin outward circles.
Cook 2–3 minutes until underside is golden and crisp and the top is dry; lower heat if browning too quickly.
Spread warm potato masala over one half, fold the dosa and crisp another 30 seconds.
Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

name: Plain Dosa
title: Plain Dosa
description: Plain Dosa, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Plain Dosa, rinse dosa rice and urad dal; soak with fenugreek and poha 4–6 hours, then drain.
Grind dal fluffy and rice smooth, adding water gradually; mix with salt and ferment covered 8–12 hours until bubbly.
Stir batter gently and thin with a little water until it pours in a steady ribbon.
Heat a seasoned tawa to medium-high and wipe with sesame oil.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread thinly in outward circles, leaving no thick centre.
Cook 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and releases easily; fold without filling.
Serve immediately with chutney and sambar.

name: Onion Uttapam
title: Onion Uttapam
description: Onion Uttapam, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Onion Uttapam, rinse idli rice and urad dal; soak with fenugreek and poha 4–6 hours, then drain.
Grind dal fluffy and rice smooth, adding water gradually; mix with salt and ferment covered 8–12 hours until bubbly and doubled.
Stir the batter gently; keep it thick enough to mound on a spoon rather than run.
Heat a seasoned tawa on medium and wipe lightly with oil.
Pour a ladle in the centre and spread only a little so the uttapam stays thick; scatter onion, chilli and coriander on top.
Cook covered 3–4 minutes until top sets and underside is golden; flip briefly to soften onion.
Serve hot with coconut chutney.

name: Pongal
title: Pongal
description: Pongal, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Pongal, rinse rice and moong dal together; dry-roast the dal on low 2 minutes until nutty but not browned.
Pressure-cook rice and dal with water and salt for 3 whistles, then mash lightly until porridge-soft.
Crush peppercorns and cumin; slice ginger and halve cashews.
Heat ghee, fry cashews golden, then add cumin, pepper, ginger and curry leaves for 30 seconds.
Pour tempering over the Pongal and stir until glossy; loosen with hot water if it stiffens.
Taste for salt and pepper and keep covered until serving.
Serve hot with coconut chutney and sambar.

name: Upma
title: Upma
description: Upma, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Upma, measure rava or broken wheat and finely chop onion, chilli, ginger and vegetables.
Dry-roast rava over low heat 4–5 minutes until aromatic; for dalia, toast 3 minutes then rinse.
Heat oil or ghee, crackle mustard and urad dal, then sauté curry leaves, chilli, ginger and onion 3 minutes.
Add diced vegetables, turmeric and salt and cook 3 minutes until they begin to soften.
Pour in boiling water carefully, then rain in the grain while stirring to avoid lumps.
Cover on low 5–8 minutes until tender with no water pooling; fluff with a fork.
Finish with coriander and lemon and serve hot.

name: Poha
title: Poha
description: Poha, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Poha, rinse thick poha briefly in a sieve, drain and rest 5 minutes until soft but still holding shape.
Boil diced potato 5 minutes until just tender; drain and reserve.
Heat oil, crackle mustard, fry peanuts until crisp, then add curry leaves, chilli and onion; sauté until translucent.
Stir in potato, turmeric and salt and cook 2 minutes so it absorbs the tempering.
Add poha and toss gently over low heat 3–4 minutes until steaming throughout without breaking the flakes.
Turn off heat, fold in lemon juice and coriander; taste and adjust salt.
Serve warm with extra lemon.

name: Vegetable Pulao
title: Vegetable Pulao
description: Vegetable Pulao, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Vegetable Pulao, rinse basmati rice until clear, soak 20 minutes, then drain; cut the vegetables into even pieces.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot; fry cumin until fragrant, then sauté onion and ginger-garlic until light gold.
Add {name}, turmeric and garam masala; stir 2 minutes so the masala coats without breaking paneer.
Add drained rice and stir gently 1 minute until grains look glossy.
Add measured water and salt; bring to a boil, cover and cook on lowest flame 12–15 minutes.
Switch off once water is absorbed and rice tender; rest covered 10 minutes, then fluff gently.
Scatter coriander and serve with raita.

name: Lemon Rice
title: Lemon Rice
description: Lemon Rice, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Lemon Rice, cook rice until tender but separate; spread on a tray to cool and prevent clumping.
For Tamarind Rice, simmer tamarind pulp with jaggery and salt until glossy; for Lemon Rice, squeeze fresh lemon and keep aside.
Heat sesame oil; crackle mustard, then fry chana dal, urad dal and peanuts until golden.
Add dried chilli, curry leaves and turmeric; stir briefly on low so spices do not scorch.
Add tamarind reduction and simmer 2 minutes, or turn off the flame before adding lemon juice.
Fold cooled rice through the tempering gently; taste and correct salt or sourness.
Rest 10 minutes and serve with papad or yogurt.

name: Tomato Rice
title: Tomato Rice
description: Tomato Rice, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Tomato Rice, rinse basmati rice until clear, soak 15 minutes and drain; chop tomatoes and slice onion.
Heat oil, crackle mustard and cumin, then sauté onion pale gold; add ginger-garlic for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, chilli and coriander powder; cook medium 8–10 minutes until tomatoes soften and oil shows.
Stir in rice until coated, add water and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer lowest flame 12–15 minutes until rice is tender and liquid absorbed.
Rest covered 10 minutes, then fluff gently without crushing the grains.
Garnish with coriander and serve with plain yogurt.

name: Curd Rice
title: Curd Rice
description: Curd Rice, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Curd Rice, rinse rice and cook with water until very soft; mash lightly while warm and cool until lukewarm, not steaming.
Whisk yogurt, milk and salt smooth, then fold through the cooled rice for a creamy texture.
Heat oil; crackle mustard and urad dal, then add green chilli and curry leaves.
Cool the tempering briefly and pour over the rice; mix gently so the rice remains creamy.
Loosen with a splash of milk if it thickens; do not heat yogurt after mixing.
Chill 20 minutes or serve at room temperature; add pomegranate just before serving.
Serve with pickle as a cooling meal.

name: Tamarind Rice
title: Tamarind Rice
description: Tamarind Rice, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Tamarind Rice, cook rice until tender but separate; spread on a tray to cool and prevent clumping.
For Tamarind Rice, simmer tamarind pulp with jaggery and salt until glossy; for Lemon Rice, squeeze fresh lemon and keep aside.
Heat sesame oil; crackle mustard, then fry chana dal, urad dal and peanuts until golden.
Add dried chilli, curry leaves and turmeric; stir briefly on low so spices do not scorch.
Add tamarind reduction and simmer 2 minutes, or turn off the flame before adding lemon juice.
Fold cooled rice through the tempering gently; taste and correct salt or sourness.
Rest 10 minutes and serve with papad or yogurt.

name: Vegetable Fried Rice
title: Vegetable Fried Rice
description: Vegetable Fried Rice, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
ingredients: 1 cup cabbage, carrot and beans, finely chopped
instructions: For Vegetable Fried Rice, use fully chilled cooked rice and separate the grains; finely chop the vegetables and slice spring onions.
Heat a wok until very hot, add oil and stir-fry vegetables 2–3 minutes until crisp-tender.
Add minced ginger and the white parts of spring onion; toss 30 seconds over high flame.
Add rice by handfuls, breaking clumps with the spatula; toss 2–3 minutes until steaming hot.
Season with soy sauce, vinegar, salt and pepper, tossing so the grains are evenly coated.
Taste and adjust seasoning; keep the vegetables bright and avoid adding water.
Fold through spring onion greens and serve immediately while the rice remains separate.

name: Chicken Fried Rice
title: Chicken Fried Rice
description: Chicken Fried Rice, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Chicken Fried Rice, use fully chilled cooked rice and separate the grains; finely dice chicken and slice spring onions.
Heat half the oil in a hot wok; scramble eggs just until set, then lift them onto a plate.
Add remaining oil and stir-fry chicken 5–7 minutes until opaque and cooked through to 74°C.
Add spring onion whites and toss 30 seconds over high flame.
Add rice by handfuls, breaking clumps; toss 2–3 minutes until steaming hot.
Return egg and season with soy sauce, vinegar, salt and pepper; toss evenly.
Fold through spring onion greens and serve immediately while the grains stay separate.

name: Egg Fried Rice
title: Egg Fried Rice
description: Egg Fried Rice, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Egg Fried Rice, use fully chilled cooked rice and separate the grains; beat the eggs and dice the carrot and peas.
Heat half the oil in a hot wok; scramble eggs just until set, then lift them onto a plate.
Add remaining oil and stir-fry carrot and peas 2–3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Add spring onion whites and toss 30 seconds over high flame.
Add rice by handfuls, breaking clumps; toss 2–3 minutes until steaming hot.
Return egg and season with soy sauce, vinegar, salt and pepper; toss evenly.
Fold through spring onion greens and serve immediately while the grains stay separate.

name: Vegetable Biryani
title: Vegetable Biryani
description: Vegetable Biryani, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Vegetable Biryani, rinse basmati until clear and soak 20 minutes; cut vegetables into even pieces so they finish together.
Fry onion in ghee until golden; add ginger-garlic, yogurt, biryani masala and turmeric and cook until masala thickens.
Fold in vegetables and salt; cover and cook 5–7 minutes until just tender, not soft.
Boil rice with cardamom, bay leaf and cloves until 70% cooked; drain while the centre is still firm.
Layer rice over vegetables with mint, coriander and fried onion; drizzle ghee over the top.
Seal and cook on a tawa over low heat 20–25 minutes; rest sealed 10 minutes before opening.
Fluff carefully and serve with raita.

name: Chicken Biryani
title: Chicken Biryani
description: Chicken Biryani, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Chicken Biryani, rinse basmati until clear and soak 20 minutes; marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic, biryani masala, chilli, turmeric, lemon and salt for 30 minutes.
Fry sliced onion in ghee until deep golden and reserve half; add marinated chicken and cook until the outside is sealed.
Boil rice in salted water with cardamom, bay leaf and cloves until 70% cooked; a grain should break with a firm white centre. Drain immediately.
Layer half the rice over chicken; scatter mint, coriander and fried onion, add remaining rice and drizzle ghee.
Seal the pot tightly and cook on a tawa over low flame 25–35 minutes; do not lift the lid during dum.
Rest sealed 10 minutes; chicken must reach 74°C at the thickest piece and rice should be tender, not mushy.
Lift from the side to preserve layers and serve with raita.

name: Egg Biryani
title: Egg Biryani
description: Egg Biryani, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Egg Biryani, rinse basmati until clear and soak 20 minutes; score boiled eggs and coat lightly with yogurt, biryani masala and turmeric.
Fry sliced onion in ghee until deep golden; reserve half and toss eggs briefly in the remaining spice oil.
Boil rice in salted water with cardamom, bay leaf and cloves until 70% cooked; a grain should break with a firm white centre. Drain immediately.
Layer eggs and half the rice; scatter mint, coriander and fried onion, then cover with remaining rice and ghee.
Seal the pot and cook on a tawa over low flame for 20–25 minutes; keep the lid closed for dum.
Rest 10 minutes; check grains are tender and eggs hot through without breaking.
Lift gently to preserve the layers and serve with raita.

name: Paneer Pulao
title: Paneer Pulao
description: Paneer Pulao, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Paneer Pulao, rinse basmati rice until clear, soak 20 minutes, then drain; cut the Paneer into even pieces.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot; fry cumin until fragrant, then sauté onion and ginger-garlic until light gold.
Add {name}, turmeric and garam masala; stir 2 minutes so the masala coats without breaking paneer.
Add drained rice and stir gently 1 minute until grains look glossy.
Add measured water and salt; bring to a boil, cover and cook on lowest flame 12–15 minutes.
Switch off once water is absorbed and rice tender; rest covered 10 minutes, then fluff gently.
Scatter coriander and serve with raita.

name: Chapati
title: Chapati
description: Chapati, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Chapati, whisk atta and salt; add warm water gradually and bring the flour together.
Knead 7–8 minutes until soft and smooth; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Divide into balls and roll each on a lightly floured surface into a thin 15 cm circle.
Heat a tawa over medium-high until a water drop sizzles; place one chapati.
Cook until bubbles appear, flip and cook until brown spots form; turn once more and press gently to puff.
Remove as soon as it puffs; overcooking makes the bread dry.
Brush with ghee if desired and keep covered in a cloth-lined box.

name: Aloo Paratha
title: Aloo Paratha
description: Aloo Paratha, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Aloo Paratha, knead atta, water and salt into a soft dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Mash potato or grate paneer; mix with chilli, cumin, amchur, coriander and salt until dry and lump-free.
Divide dough and filling evenly; seal each filling ball inside a dough cup.
Dust lightly and roll gently to a 16 cm round, turning so filling does not tear the surface.
Cook on a hot tawa over medium until bubbles form; flip and brush with ghee.
Turn again and cook until both sides have brown blisters and centre is hot, about 2 minutes each side.
Serve straight from tawa with yogurt or pickle.

name: Paneer Paratha
title: Paneer Paratha
description: Paneer Paratha, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Paneer Paratha, knead atta, water and salt into a soft dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.

name: Poori Masala
title: Poori Masala
description: Poori Masala, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Poori Masala, knead atta, salt and water into a firm smooth dough; cover and rest 15 minutes.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in oil; sauté onion until soft, then add turmeric and salt.
Add boiled potato and water; simmer 5 minutes, mashing a few pieces to thicken the masala.
Divide dough and roll into evenly thick 10 cm circles.
Heat oil to about 180°C; slide in a poori and press gently until it puffs.
Turn once, fry pale golden and drain; cool oil makes pooris greasy.
Serve immediately with potato masala.

name: Chole Bhature
title: Chole Bhature
description: Chole Bhature, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Chole Bhature, soak chickpeas overnight, drain and pressure-cook with salt until soft but intact; reserve cooking liquid.
Knead maida, yogurt, salt and baking powder into a soft dough; cover and ferment 2–3 hours.
Fry onion until golden; add ginger-garlic, tomatoes and chole masala and cook until thick with oil at the edges.
Add chickpeas and cooking liquid; simmer 15 minutes and crush a few beans to thicken the gravy.
Divide bhatura dough, roll into ovals and rest 5 minutes as oil heats to 180°C.
Fry each bhatura, pressing lightly until puffed; turn once and drain when golden.
Finish chole with coriander and lemon and serve hot with bhature.

name: Pav Bhaji
title: Pav Bhaji
description: Pav Bhaji, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Pav Bhaji, pressure-cook potatoes, cauliflower and peas until very soft; drain but reserve cooking liquid.
Heat butter on a tawa, sauté onion and capsicum until soft, then add tomatoes and pav bhaji masala.
Cook 8 minutes until tomatoes break down and butter appears at the edges.
Add vegetables and mash firmly on the tawa, adding reserved liquid to keep bhaji moist.
Simmer and mash 8–10 minutes until no large pieces remain; correct salt and lemon.
Toast split pav with butter on a second hot pan until golden at the cut sides.
Top bhaji with butter, onion and coriander; serve with pav and lemon.

name: Kathi Roll
title: Kathi Roll
description: Kathi Roll, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Kathi Roll, cut and season the paneer filling with the listed masala, salt and oil; keep pieces small for an even cook.
Cook the paneer over medium-high until browned and done; chicken must reach 74°C, paneer should be golden, and egg fully set.
Warm each paratha or wrap on a tawa until flexible.
Spread mint chutney or ketchup down the centre and add the hot filling in a narrow strip.
Top with onion, cucumber or lemon as listed; keep the filling centred so the wrap closes.
Fold the bottom edge up and roll tightly; secure in paper if carrying.
Serve hot while bread is soft and filling juicy.

title: Egg Roll

name: Vegetable Sandwich
title: Vegetable Sandwich
description: Vegetable Sandwich, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Vegetable Sandwich, boil and cool potato; slice it, cucumber and tomato thinly and pat vegetables dry.
Butter bread lightly and spread coriander chutney on the inner sides.
Layer potato, cucumber and tomato; sprinkle chaat masala and salt lightly.
Close with the second slice and press gently so the layers hold.
Toast on a buttered tawa over medium 2–3 minutes per side until crisp and golden, or leave untoasted.
Cut diagonally with a serrated knife to avoid squeezing out filling.
Serve immediately with chutney.

name: Masala Khichdi
title: Masala Khichdi
description: Masala Khichdi, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Masala Khichdi, rinse rice and moong dal together and soak 10 minutes; chop vegetables evenly.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle cumin, then sauté onion, ginger and chilli until fragrant.
Add vegetables, turmeric and salt and stir 2 minutes.
Add drained rice and dal with measured water; mix once and lock the cooker.
Cook 3 whistles and allow pressure to release naturally; grains should be soft and creamy.
Stir, adjust salt and loosen with hot water if needed; finish with garam masala and coriander.
Serve hot with yogurt, pickle and ghee.

name: Sprouts Salad
title: Sprouts Salad
description: Sprouts Salad, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Sprouts Salad, cook or steam the main ingredient for Sprouts Salad until tender but not mushy; drain and cool completely.
Dice cucumber, tomato and onion finely so each spoonful has an even mix.
Whisk lemon juice with roasted cumin, chaat masala and salt; add oil for a light dressing.
Toss cooled legumes, corn or sweet potato with dressing first so seasoning reaches the centre.
Fold in chopped vegetables and coriander gently; avoid crushing beans.
Rest 5 minutes, then taste and adjust lemon, salt and chilli.
Serve at room temperature; keep dressing separate if preparing ahead.

name: Millet Vegetable Bowl
title: Millet Vegetable Bowl
description: Millet Vegetable Bowl, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Millet Vegetable Bowl, rinse the foxtail millet and cook by absorption until tender; rest covered 5 minutes and fluff.
Cut vegetables evenly and steam until just tender with a little salt so they retain shape.
Heat oil and toast cumin; add vegetables and toss 1–2 minutes with salt.
For ragi, stir often and add water gradually to avoid lumps; quinoa generally cooks in 15 minutes and should retain a slight bite.
Spoon the cooked grain into bowls and arrange vegetables on top to preserve separate textures.
Finish with lemon, coriander and roasted cumin dressing; correct salt.
Serve warm with yogurt or chutney if desired.

title: Vegetable Dal Khichdi
description: Vegetable Dal Khichdi, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Vegetable Dal Khichdi, rinse rice and moong dal; soak 10 minutes while cutting the mixed vegetables evenly.
Heat ghee in a pressure cooker and crackle cumin until aromatic.
Add vegetables, turmeric and salt; stir for 2 minutes to coat with the seasoning.
Add drained rice, dal and measured water; stir once and lock the cooker.
Cook for 3 whistles, then allow pressure to release naturally; rice and dal should be soft and creamy.
Stir well and adjust salt or loosen with hot water; the khichdi should be spoonable.
Finish with coriander and serve hot.

name: Spinach Dal Bowl
title: Spinach Dal Bowl
description: Spinach Dal Bowl, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Spinach Dal Bowl, rinse toor dal and soak 10 minutes; wash and chop spinach while it softens.
Pressure-cook dal with turmeric and water until completely soft, then mash smooth.
Heat ghee in a pan and crackle cumin; add garlic and green chilli and stir until fragrant.
Add spinach and cook 2–3 minutes until wilted, then stir in the cooked dal.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes until the dal thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Taste and adjust salt; add a little hot water if it becomes too thick.
Finish with lemon and coriander and serve hot.

name: Sambar Rice
title: Sambar Rice
description: Sambar Rice, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Sambar Rice, rinse rice and toor dal; pressure-cook with turmeric and water until both are soft, about 3 whistles.
Prepare the chosen base: simmer vegetables with tamarind and sambar powder for Sambar Rice, or tomato with tamarind and rasam powder for Rasam Rice.
For rasam rice, crush pepper, cumin and garlic and add to the simmering broth; for sambar rice, cook vegetables until tender before adding dal.
Stir the cooked rice and dal into the seasoned broth and add hot water to a soft spoonable consistency.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in ghee and pour over; simmer the mixed rice 3 minutes so flavours meld.
Taste for salt and tang; the grains should be soft but the dish should not be watery.
Finish with coriander and serve hot with papad.

name: Rasam Rice
title: Rasam Rice
description: Rasam Rice, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Rasam Rice, rinse rice and toor dal; pressure-cook with turmeric and water until both are soft, about 3 whistles.
Prepare the chosen base: simmer vegetables with tamarind and sambar powder for Sambar Rice, or tomato with tamarind and rasam powder for Rasam Rice.

name: Curd Millet Bowl
title: Curd Millet Bowl
description: Curd Millet Bowl, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Curd Millet Bowl, rinse millet and cook with water until tender and separate; spread on a plate to cool until lukewarm.
Whisk yogurt, milk and salt until smooth.
Fold yogurt into cooled millet; do not add it while the grain is steaming hot.
Heat oil, crackle mustard and add chilli and curry leaves.
Cool tempering briefly, then fold into the millet; add pomegranate if listed.
Adjust consistency with milk and chill 15 minutes.
Serve cold with pickle.

name: Paneer Salad Bowl
title: Paneer Salad Bowl
description: Paneer Salad Bowl, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Paneer Salad Bowl, cut paneer into even cubes and pat dry; toss with cumin, salt and a little oil.
Dice cucumber and tomato, slice onion thinly, and keep the vegetables cool and dry.
Sear paneer in a medium-hot pan 2 minutes per side until golden at the edges.
Whisk lemon juice and chaat masala into a light dressing.
Arrange the vegetables in bowls and add warm paneer on top.
Taste for salt and acidity; add coriander and extra lemon if needed.
Serve at once while the paneer is warm.

name: Grilled Chicken Salad
title: Grilled Chicken Salad
description: Grilled Chicken Salad, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Grilled Chicken Salad, pat chicken dry and coat with yogurt, cumin, salt, oil and lemon juice; marinate 20 minutes.
Cook brown rice until tender for the bowl; wash and dry cucumber, tomato and lettuce.
Heat a grill pan over medium-high; cook chicken 5–7 minutes per side until browned and 74°C at the centre.
Rest chicken 5 minutes, then slice across the grain so it stays juicy.
Arrange vegetables over warm rice for the bowl, or over lettuce for the salad.
Add chicken and drizzle with the listed lemon juice just before serving.
Taste for salt and serve warm.

name: Egg Protein Bowl
title: Egg Protein Bowl
description: Egg Protein Bowl, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Egg Protein Bowl, boil eggs 9 minutes for firm yolks; cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Drain cooked chickpeas and season while slightly warm with salt and cumin.
Chop cucumber, tomato and onion and toss with lemon, coriander and chaat masala.
Spoon chickpeas into bowls and arrange the chopped salad alongside.
Add egg halves and sprinkle with black pepper if available.
Taste the salad for acidity and add lemon if needed.
Serve immediately; keep eggs refrigerated if preparing ahead.

name: Mixed Vegetable Bowl
title: Mixed Vegetable Bowl
description: Mixed Vegetable Bowl, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Mixed Vegetable Bowl, rinse the brown rice and cook by absorption until tender; rest covered 5 minutes and fluff.
Cut vegetables evenly and steam until just tender with a little salt so they retain shape.
Heat oil and toast cumin; add vegetables and toss 1–2 minutes with salt.
For ragi, stir often and add water gradually to avoid lumps; quinoa generally cooks in 15 minutes and should retain a slight bite.
Spoon the cooked grain into bowls and arrange vegetables on top to preserve separate textures.
Finish with lemon, coriander and roasted cumin dressing; correct salt.
Serve warm with yogurt or chutney if desired.

name: Sweet Potato Chaat
title: Sweet Potato Chaat
description: Sweet Potato Chaat, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Sweet Potato Chaat, cook or steam the main ingredient for Sweet Potato Chaat until tender but not mushy; drain and cool completely.
Dice cucumber, tomato and onion finely so each spoonful has an even mix.
Whisk lemon juice with roasted cumin, chaat masala and salt; add oil for a light dressing.
Toss cooled legumes, corn or sweet potato with dressing first so seasoning reaches the centre.
Fold in chopped vegetables and coriander gently; avoid crushing beans.
Rest 5 minutes, then taste and adjust lemon, salt and chilli.
Serve at room temperature; keep dressing separate if preparing ahead.

name: Corn Salad
title: Corn Salad
description: Corn Salad, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Corn Salad, cook or steam the main ingredient for Corn Salad until tender but not mushy; drain and cool completely.

name: Gulab Jamun
title: Gulab Jamun
description: Gulab Jamun, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
ingredients: 4 cups ghee or oil for frying
instructions: For Gulab Jamun, simmer sugar and water with cardamom 6–8 minutes until clear and lightly sticky; keep the syrup warm, not boiling.
Crumble khoya finely, sift in maida and add ghee; sprinkle milk a teaspoon at a time to make a soft dough without kneading hard.
Rest 10 minutes, then roll smooth crack-free balls; cracks can split in hot ghee.
Heat ghee on low; a test crumb should rise slowly without browning immediately.
Fry balls gently, turning continuously for 8–10 minutes until evenly deep golden and cooked through.
Drain briefly and soak in warm syrup at least 45 minutes, turning once so centres absorb it.
Serve warm; add rose water to syrup only if using.

name: Rasmalai
title: Rasmalai
description: Rasmalai, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Rasmalai, bring chhena milk to a boil, switch off and add lemon juice gradually until whey separates; strain and rinse the chhena.
Hang chhena 30 minutes and knead until smooth; shape into small flat discs with no cracks.
Simmer sugar and water in a wide pan; add discs, cover and cook briskly 12–15 minutes until expanded.
In a second pan, simmer rabri milk on low, scraping the sides until reduced by one-third; stir in sugar and cardamom.
Lift discs gently, press out excess syrup and slide into warm rabri; chill at least 2 hours.
Check discs are springy and soaked through, not dense at the centre.
Garnish with pistachios and serve cold.

name: Kheer
title: Kheer
description: Kheer, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Kheer, rinse rice and soak 15 minutes; for semiya, separate the strands and measure them before heating the milk.
Bring milk to a gentle boil in a heavy pan, stirring the base so it does not catch.
Add rice and simmer low 25–35 minutes, stirring often, until grains are very soft; semiya needs only 8–10 minutes after roasting in ghee.
For Phirni, grind soaked rice coarsely and whisk into milk; cook until the mixture coats a spoon.
Stir in sugar and cardamom and simmer 3 minutes until dissolved.
Fry cashews and raisins in ghee until golden and fold through.
Serve warm or chill until set; phirni is traditionally served cold.

title: Rice Payasam
description: Rice Payasam, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.

name: Carrot Halwa
title: Carrot Halwa
description: Carrot Halwa, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Carrot Halwa, peel and grate carrots; for Badam Halwa, blanch almonds, peel and grind with a little milk to a smooth paste.
Heat ghee in a heavy kadai; sauté carrots 6–8 minutes until their raw smell fades, or cook almond paste over low heat, stirring constantly.
Add milk and simmer carrots until tender and most liquid evaporates; almond paste should thicken and pull away from the pan.
Add sugar and cardamom; stir as the mixture loosens, then thickens again.
Cook until glossy and ghee releases at the edges; keep the flame low to prevent scorching.
Toast cashews and raisins in ghee and fold through.
Serve warm; carrot halwa can also be chilled and reheated gently.

name: Badam Halwa
title: Badam Halwa
description: Badam Halwa, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.

name: Mysore Pak
title: Mysore Pak
description: Mysore Pak, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Mysore Pak, sift besan and warm ghee until liquid but not smoking.
Simmer sugar and water to a one-string syrup; a drop between fingers should form a fine thread.
Lower the flame and whisk in besan gradually until smooth.
Add warm ghee one spoon at a time, stirring continuously over medium-low heat as it foams and absorbs.
Cook until porous, fragrant and releasing ghee at the edges; do not wait for a dark colour.
Pour into a greased tray and score squares while warm.
Cool completely before cutting and serving.

name: Jangiri
title: Jangiri
description: Jangiri, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
ingredients: 2 cups ghee or oil for frying
instructions: For Jangiri, make a light one-string syrup by simmering sugar and water 6–8 minutes; add cardamom and lemon and keep warm.
For Jalebi, ferment maida, yogurt and yeast batter until bubbly; for Jangiri, grind soaked urad dal to a fluffy paste and mix rice flour.
Load a piping cloth and test a spiral; batter should hold its shape without spreading.
Heat ghee or oil to medium (about 170°C) and pipe small spirals carefully.
Fry slowly, turning once, until crisp and evenly golden; lower heat if the centre remains pale.
Lift directly into warm syrup for 30–45 seconds, turning once, then drain.
Serve warm and crisp the same day.

title: Jalebi

name: Kaju Katli
title: Kaju Katli
description: Kaju Katli, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Kaju Katli, pulse cashews to a fine powder, stopping before they release oil.
Boil sugar and water 4–5 minutes until sticky and thread-forming.
Add cashew powder and stir on low until it forms a soft dough and leaves the pan.
Cool until safe to handle, knead briefly with ghee, then roll between parchment to 4–5 mm thickness.
Apply silver leaf if using and allow the sheet to set 20 minutes.
Cut into diamonds with a sharp knife.
Cool fully and store airtight.

name: Coconut Ladoo
title: Coconut Ladoo
description: Coconut Ladoo, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Coconut Ladoo, measure grated coconut, condensed milk, ghee, cardamom and chopped pistachios.
Warm ghee in a heavy pan over low heat; add coconut and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in condensed milk and cook on low, stirring continuously, until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan.
Stir in cardamom and pistachios, then remove from heat.
Cool until safe to handle but still pliable, about 10 minutes.
Grease your palms lightly and shape equal balls; press gently so they hold without compacting.
Cool completely and store airtight in the refrigerator.

name: Besan Ladoo
title: Besan Ladoo
description: Besan Ladoo, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Besan Ladoo, sift besan to remove lumps and measure ghee, powdered sugar, cardamom and chopped almonds.
Melt ghee in a heavy pan over low heat; add besan and stir continuously.
Roast 15–20 minutes until the flour smells nutty and turns a deeper golden colour; do not raise the flame.
Remove from heat and cool until warm, about 15 minutes, so sugar will not melt.
Mix in powdered sugar, cardamom and almonds until evenly combined.
Press a little mixture in your palm; it should hold together without crumbling.
Shape equal ladoos while warm and let set fully before storing airtight.

name: Rava Kesari
title: Rava Kesari
description: Rava Kesari, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Rava Kesari, bring water, sugar and saffron to a boil; keep the syrup hot beside the pan.
Heat ghee, fry cashews and raisins golden, and remove.
Add rava and roast over low heat 4–5 minutes until aromatic but still pale.
Pour hot syrup in a thin stream while stirring vigorously to prevent lumps.
Cook low 3–5 minutes until rava swells and leaves the pan sides.
Stir in cardamom and toasted nuts; cover 2 minutes.
Serve warm while soft and glossy.

name: Adhirasam
title: Adhirasam
description: Adhirasam, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Adhirasam, melt jaggery with water and strain; simmer briefly to a soft syrup and cool until warm.
For Modak, cook coconut and jaggery filling until moist but not wet; for Unniyappam, mash ripe banana into the batter instead.
For Modak, boil water with salt and ghee, stir in rice flour, cover 5 minutes and knead warm; for Adhirasam, mix jaggery syrup into rice flour and rest overnight.
Shape pleated modaks around filling; form adhirasam into discs or pour unniyappam batter into greased paniyaram wells.
Steam modak 10–12 minutes until glossy; fry adhirasam or unniyappam over medium-low until browned and cooked through.
Check one fried sweet at the centre before removing; drain on a rack.
Serve modak warm and cool fried sweets before storing.

name: Peda
title: Peda
description: Peda, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Peda, mix milk powder and condensed milk in a heavy pan until no dry patches remain.
Cook on low, stirring and scraping continuously until the mixture thickens into a soft dough.
Add ghee and cardamom; cook until the mass leaves the sides but remains pliable.
Cool until warm enough to handle, then knead briefly until smooth.
Divide and shape into small discs, pressing a pistachio into each centre.
Let set at room temperature 1–2 hours.
Store airtight once cool.

name: Sandesh
title: Sandesh
description: Sandesh, a much-loved East Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Sandesh, bring milk just to a boil, switch off and add lemon juice gradually until whey separates; strain and rinse chhena.
Hang 20 minutes so chhena stays soft; knead on a plate until smooth and free of grains.
Warm chhena and sugar together in a heavy pan over low heat, stirring continuously.
Cook 4–6 minutes until mixture gathers and leaves the pan; overcooking makes Sandesh dry and grainy.
Cool until warm, knead briefly with cardamom and shape into discs or moulds.
Press pistachios into each piece if using; let set at room temperature.
Serve fresh or chilled the same day.

name: Rasgulla
title: Rasgulla
description: Rasgulla, a much-loved East Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Rasgulla, bring milk just to a boil, switch off and add lemon juice gradually until whey separates; strain through muslin and rinse chhena until the whey runs clear.
Hang chhena 30 minutes, then knead until smooth and grain-free; stop before it becomes oily.
Shape 10–12 smooth crack-free balls; cracks may split when syrup boils.
Boil sugar and water in a wide pan; add balls, cover and simmer briskly 12–15 minutes until doubled.
Do not stir; swirl the pan gently once so the balls cook evenly and stay round.
Press one lightly: it should spring back and have no dense centre; cool in syrup.
Serve chilled with a little syrup.

name: Shrikhand
title: Shrikhand
description: Shrikhand, a much-loved West Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Shrikhand, tie yogurt in clean muslin and hang in the refrigerator 6–8 hours until thick hung curd remains.
Soak saffron in warm milk 10 minutes until the milk turns golden.
Whisk hung curd smooth and add powdered sugar in batches until dissolved.
Fold in cardamom and saffron milk; taste and adjust sweetness.
Chill at least 1 hour so the dessert firms and flavours meld.
Garnish with pistachios just before serving.
Serve cold with puri or as dessert.

name: Kulfi
title: Kulfi
description: Kulfi, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Kulfi, bring milk to a simmer in a wide heavy pan and reduce over low heat, scraping the sides every few minutes.
After 30–40 minutes, when milk has reduced by about half and coats a spoon, add sugar and milk powder.
Stir smooth, then add cardamom and pistachios.
Cool completely and pour into kulfi moulds, leaving a little headspace.
Freeze 2 hours, insert sticks when partly set, then freeze at least 6 more hours.
Check firmness through the mould; the centre must be frozen solid.
Dip moulds briefly in warm water to release and serve immediately.

name: Falooda
title: Falooda
description: Falooda, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Falooda, soak basil seeds in water 15 minutes until swollen and gel-like; drain.
Boil falooda sev until tender (usually 4–5 minutes), rinse cold and drain well.
Chill milk and rose syrup; stir sugar into the milk until dissolved.
Layer basil seeds and sev in tall glasses and pour over rose milk.
Add rose ice cream and drizzle rose syrup over the top.
Scatter chopped nuts and serve with a long spoon and straw.
Assemble just before serving so the sev does not turn mushy.

name: Double Ka Meetha
title: Double Ka Meetha
description: Double Ka Meetha, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Double Ka Meetha, cut bread into triangles and leave uncovered 30 minutes to dry slightly.
Fry in ghee over medium heat until crisp and deep golden on both sides; drain.
Simmer milk with sugar and cardamom until reduced by one-third and coats a spoon.
Arrange fried bread in a shallow dish and pour over the warm reduced milk.
Toast cashews and raisins in a little ghee and scatter over the bread.
Rest 10 minutes so the bread absorbs the milk without losing all its crisp edges.
Serve warm or chilled.

name: Soan Papdi
title: Soan Papdi
description: Soan Papdi, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Soan Papdi, sift besan and maida together; warm ghee until liquid.
Cook sugar, water and lemon juice to hard-ball stage (about 130°C); a drop in cold water should form a firm pliable ball.
Cool syrup slightly and beat with a spatula until pale and fibrous; take care because it is hot.
Fold in flour mixture and warm ghee in batches, pulling and folding to build fine strands.
Press lightly into a greased tray without compacting the layers.
Scatter pistachios and score squares while warm.
Cool fully before separating flaky pieces.

name: Unniyappam
title: Unniyappam
description: Unniyappam, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Unniyappam, melt jaggery with water and strain; simmer briefly to a soft syrup and cool until warm.
