name: Sambar
title: Sambar
description: Sambar, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
ingredients: 1 cup drumstick, carrot and pumpkin pieces
instructions: For Sambar, rinse toor dal and pressure-cook with turmeric and water for 3 whistles; mash until smooth.
Cut drumstick, carrot and pumpkin evenly; simmer with salt until just tender, about 10 minutes.
Add tamarind pulp and sambar powder; boil 5 minutes so the raw tamarind aroma fades.
Stir in mashed dal and simmer gently until the vegetables are fully tender and the broth lightly coats a spoon.
Temper mustard, dried chilli and curry leaves in hot oil until the seeds pop; pour over the sambar.
Taste and adjust salt and tang; add hot water if the sambar is too thick.
Finish with coriander and serve with rice or idli.

name: Rasam
title: Rasam
description: Rasam, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Rasam, soak tamarind in warm water 10 minutes and extract pulp; crush pepper, cumin and garlic coarsely.
Simmer tomato, tamarind water, turmeric and rasam powder until tomato collapses and raw sourness softens.
Add cooked toor dal and water and heat until frothy at the edges; avoid a hard boil.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in ghee, add crushed pepper-cumin and garlic, then pour into rasam.
Taste for salt and tang; dilute with hot water if too sharp.
Cover for 2 minutes so the pepper aroma infuses.
Garnish with coriander and serve immediately.

name: Avial
title: Avial
description: Avial, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, yam, drumstick)
instructions: For Avial, cut carrot, beans, yam and drumstick into long even batons; keep harder vegetables slightly smaller.
Simmer vegetables with turmeric, salt and a little water until tender but still holding shape.
Grind coconut, cumin and green chilli coarsely with a splash of water.
Fold coconut paste into vegetables and simmer 3 minutes on low.
Whisk yogurt smooth and stir in off the heat to prevent curdling.
Drizzle coconut oil and add curry leaves; cover 5 minutes.
Serve thick as a Kerala rice side.

name: Poriyal
title: Poriyal
description: Poriyal, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
ingredients: 2 cups finely chopped cabbage or beans
instructions: For Poriyal, wash and finely chop cabbage or beans; drain well so they stir-fry rather than steam.
Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard, then fry urad dal and dried chilli until dal turns pale gold.
Add curry leaves, vegetables, turmeric and salt; toss over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Cover and cook on low 5–8 minutes, stirring once, until tender but not mushy.
Uncover and evaporate excess moisture; fold in grated coconut.
Taste for salt; the finished poriyal should be dry and lightly crisp.
Serve with rice and sambar.

name: Kootu
title: Kootu
description: Kootu, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
ingredients: 1 cup diced pumpkin or bottle gourd
instructions: For Kootu, rinse moong dal and simmer with turmeric until soft but still holding some texture.
Dice pumpkin or gourd and add to dal with salt; cook until just tender.
Grind coconut, cumin and green chilli with a spoon of water to a coarse paste.
Stir paste into dal and simmer 4–5 minutes until its raw aroma disappears.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in coconut oil and pour over the kootu.
Adjust with hot water; kootu should be thicker than sambar.
Serve with steamed rice.

name: Kara Kuzhambu
title: Kara Kuzhambu
description: Kara Kuzhambu, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Kara Kuzhambu, soak tamarind in warm water and extract a thick pulp; rinse and halve the shallots.
Heat sesame oil and crackle mustard and fenugreek; add dried chilli and curry leaves.
Add shallots and tomato and sauté until softened and lightly browned.
Stir in kuzhambu powder and turmeric for 20 seconds, then add tamarind water, salt and jaggery.
Simmer uncovered 18–25 minutes until gravy thickens and oil beads appear on the surface.
Taste for a tangy, savoury balance; add hot water if concentrated.
Serve over rice with sesame oil.

name: Vatha Kuzhambu
title: Vatha Kuzhambu
description: Vatha Kuzhambu, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Vatha Kuzhambu, soak tamarind in warm water 10 minutes and extract a thick pulp; peel shallots and measure kuzhambu powder.
Heat sesame oil; crackle mustard and fenugreek, then add dried chilli and curry leaves.
Add shallots and fry slowly until golden and sweet; keep them intact.
Stir in kuzhambu powder and turmeric briefly, then add tamarind water, salt and jaggery.
Simmer uncovered 18–25 minutes until sauce thickens and oil beads appear on top.
Taste for sharp tamarind tang balanced by jaggery; add hot water if overly concentrated.
Serve over rice with sesame oil.

name: Appam
title: Appam
description: Appam, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Appam, rinse rice and soak 4–5 hours; grind with cooked rice and grated coconut until smooth.
Dissolve yeast and sugar in lukewarm water and mix into the batter with salt.
Cover and ferment 8–10 hours until bubbly and lightly risen; thin with water until pourable.
Heat an appachatti on medium and brush lightly with oil.
Pour in a ladle and swirl to coat the sides, leaving a thicker pool in the centre.
Cover and cook 2–3 minutes until the lace is crisp and centre set and spongy; do not flip.
Lift out and serve warm with stew or coconut milk.

name: Puttu
title: Puttu
description: Puttu, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Puttu, sprinkle salt into puttu flour; add water a tablespoon at a time and rub until it resembles damp sand with no lumps.
Rest the moistened flour 10 minutes, then rub again and sieve for a light texture.
Layer coconut and damp flour alternately in the puttu cylinder, finishing with coconut; do not pack tightly.
Steam over vigorously boiling water 6–8 minutes until steam rises steadily from the top.
Push contents out carefully; puttu should hold its shape but crumble softly.
Repeat with remaining flour and coconut.
Serve hot with kadala curry, banana or ghee.

name: Idiyappam
title: Idiyappam
description: Idiyappam, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Idiyappam, bring water, salt and sesame oil to a rolling boil; add rice flour and stir quickly until it gathers into a dough.
Cover 5 minutes, then knead while warm until smooth and crack-free.
Fill an idiyappam press and squeeze fine strands into loose nests on greased idli plates.
Sprinkle coconut if using and steam over boiling water 8–10 minutes.
Check a strand: it should be tender, not chalky; over-steaming dries the nests.
Rest 2 minutes before lifting with a spatula.
Serve with stew or sweetened coconut milk.

name: Kerala Parotta
title: Kerala Parotta
description: Kerala Parotta, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Kerala Parotta, mix maida, sugar and salt; add water and oil and knead 10 minutes until elastic and very soft.
Cover with oil and rest at least 1 hour so the dough stretches without tearing.
Divide into balls, oil the surface and stretch each into a thin translucent sheet.
Brush with ghee, pleat like a paper fan, coil into rounds and rest 15 minutes.
Flatten gently and cook on a hot tawa over medium with ghee until layered and golden on both sides.
Stack 2–3 parottas and clap the edges gently to separate flaky layers.
Serve warm with Malabar curry.

name: Malabar Chicken Curry
title: Malabar Chicken Curry
description: Malabar Chicken Curry, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Malabar Chicken Curry, rinse chicken and pat dry; slice onion and measure fennel, curry leaves and coconut milk.
Heat coconut oil; crackle fennel and sauté onion until translucent, then add ginger-garlic and chilli.
Add chicken, turmeric, coriander and salt; turn pieces until coated and lightly sealed.
Pour in a splash of water, cover and simmer on low 25–30 minutes, stirring once halfway.
Check the thickest piece reaches 74°C; add coconut milk and simmer uncovered 3 minutes without a hard boil.
Taste the gravy and adjust salt; curry should be aromatic and lightly creamy.
Finish with curry leaves and serve with appam or rice.

name: Fish Curry
title: Fish Curry
description: Fish Curry, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Fish Curry, pat the fish or prawns for Fish Curry dry and season with turmeric and salt; rest 10 minutes.
Heat mustard or coconut oil and brown onion; add ginger-garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add tomato and listed ground spices; cook 6–8 minutes until soft and oil edges the masala.
Stir in tamarind water, or coconut milk for Goan prawn curry, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add potato wedges first for Macher Jhol and simmer until nearly tender; then add fish for 8–10 minutes, or prawns for only 3–4 minutes.
Check fish flakes at the thickest part or prawns turn opaque and curl; avoid a rolling boil.
Finish with coriander and serve with steamed rice.

name: Chicken Chettinad
title: Chicken Chettinad
description: Chicken Chettinad, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Chicken Chettinad, dry-roast coriander, fennel, peppercorns, poppy seeds and dried chillies on low until fragrant; cool and grind coarsely.
Rinse chicken and pat dry; chop onion and tomato and measure curry leaves.
Heat oil and sauté onion until golden; add ginger-garlic and curry leaves for 30 seconds.
Add chicken, turmeric and salt; brown the pieces on medium-high for 4–5 minutes.
Stir in tomato and the ground spice paste with 1 cup water; cover and simmer low 25–30 minutes.
Check chicken reaches 74°C and the gravy is thick and peppery; reduce uncovered if needed.
Garnish with coriander and serve with rice or parotta.

name: Mutton Curry
title: Mutton Curry
description: Mutton Curry, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Mutton Curry, rinse and pat the mutton dry; coat with yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli, turmeric and salt and rest 30 minutes.
For Mutton Curry, brown onion slowly in a heavy pot; cook deeper for a dark kosha-style gravy.
Add the listed spices and tomato and sauté 8 minutes until thick and oil separates.
Add marinated meat and turn each piece in masala until no raw surfaces remain.
Add measured water, cover and simmer low for 60–75 minutes; stir every 10 minutes so the base does not catch.
Check chicken reaches 74°C or mutton yields easily to a fork; reduce uncovered if gravy is thin.
Finish with coriander or curry leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Butter Chicken
title: Butter Chicken
description: Butter Chicken, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Butter Chicken, rinse and pat the chicken dry; coat with yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli, turmeric and salt and rest 30 minutes.
For Butter Chicken, brown onion slowly in a heavy pot; cook deeper for a dark kosha-style gravy.
Add the listed spices and tomato and sauté 8 minutes until thick and oil separates.
Add marinated meat and turn each piece in masala until no raw surfaces remain.
Add measured water, cover and simmer low for 25–30 minutes; stir every 10 minutes so the base does not catch.
Check chicken reaches 74°C or mutton yields easily to a fork; reduce uncovered if gravy is thin.
Finish with coriander or curry leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Paneer Butter Masala
title: Paneer Butter Masala
description: Paneer Butter Masala, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Paneer Butter Masala, blend tomatoes smooth; chop onion and cut paneer into even 2 cm cubes.
Melt butter on medium, crackle cumin, then sauté onion until translucent; add ginger-garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli and salt; cook uncovered 10–12 minutes until thick and butter beads at the edges.
Blend the gravy until silky if desired, return to low heat and add a splash of water and cream.
Add paneer and simmer gently for 3–4 minutes only; longer boiling makes it rubbery.
Stir in garam masala and a final small knob of butter; taste for salt.
Serve hot with roti or naan.

name: Dal Makhani
title: Dal Makhani
description: Dal Makhani, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Dal Makhani, rinse urad and kidney beans, soak overnight, drain and pressure-cook in fresh water until completely soft (6–8 whistles).
Mash a small portion against the pot to thicken while leaving most beans whole.
Heat butter; sauté ginger-garlic, add tomato, chilli and salt and cook until glossy.
Add beans with cooking liquid and simmer on the lowest flame at least 30 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in garam masala and cream and cook 5 more minutes until rich and spoon-coating.
Taste for salt; add hot water if too thick.
Finish with butter and serve with naan or jeera rice.

name: Palak Paneer
title: Palak Paneer
description: Palak Paneer, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Palak Paneer, blanch spinach 2 minutes, cool in cold water, drain and blend smooth.
Sear paneer briefly in oil until lightly golden and set aside.
Heat oil, crackle cumin and sauté onion until golden; add ginger-garlic and tomato until soft.
Add spinach purée, turmeric, chilli and salt; simmer gently 5 minutes uncovered.
Fold paneer and garam masala in and simmer 3 minutes until hot through.
Turn off heat and swirl in cream; do not boil after adding it.
Serve with roti or rice.

name: Aloo Gobi
title: Aloo Gobi
description: Aloo Gobi, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Aloo Gobi, cut potatoes and cauliflower into similar pieces; rinse and dry thoroughly.
Heat oil, crackle cumin, then sauté onion and ginger until soft.
Add turmeric, coriander and chilli; stir briefly, then coat potatoes in the masala.
Cover and cook low 8 minutes, stirring once; add a splash of water only if pan is dry.
Add cauliflower and salt; cover and cook 8–10 minutes until both vegetables are tender but intact.
Uncover, add garam masala and cook 2 minutes to evaporate moisture; finish with coriander.
Serve as a dry sabzi with roti.

name: Baingan Bharta
title: Baingan Bharta
description: Baingan Bharta, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Baingan Bharta, prick eggplant and roast over flame or under a hot grill, turning until the skin chars and flesh collapses, about 15–20 minutes.
Cool, peel away charred skin and mash the smoky flesh; discard watery liquid.
Heat mustard oil until it just smokes, cool slightly, add cumin and onion and sauté golden.
Add ginger-garlic, tomato, turmeric and chilli and cook until tomatoes collapse and oil separates.
Fold in eggplant and simmer uncovered 8–10 minutes, stirring so it does not catch.
Taste for salt and smoky flavour; finish with coriander.
Serve hot with roti.

name: Rajma Masala
title: Rajma Masala
description: Rajma Masala, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Rajma Masala, soak kidney beans overnight, drain and pressure-cook with fresh water until creamy inside; reserve cooking liquid.
Heat oil and crackle cumin; sauté onion until deep gold, then add ginger-garlic.
Add tomato, turmeric, coriander and chilli; cook 8–10 minutes until thick and oil separates.
Stir in cooked {bean} and garam masala with enough cooking liquid for thick gravy.
Simmer covered low 20 minutes; crush a few beans against the side to give body.
Check beans are soft and gravy clings to a spoon; adjust salt and heat.
Garnish with coriander and serve with rice or roti.

name: Chana Masala
title: Chana Masala
description: Chana Masala, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Chana Masala, soak chickpeas overnight, drain and pressure-cook with fresh water until creamy inside; reserve cooking liquid.
Heat oil and crackle cumin; sauté onion until deep gold, then add ginger-garlic.
Add tomato, turmeric, coriander and chilli; cook 8–10 minutes until thick and oil separates.
Stir in cooked {bean} and garam masala with enough cooking liquid for thick gravy.
Simmer covered low 20 minutes; crush a few beans against the side to give body.
Check beans are soft and gravy clings to a spoon; adjust salt and heat.
Garnish with coriander and serve with rice or roti.

name: Kadhi Pakora
title: Kadhi Pakora
description: Kadhi Pakora, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Kadhi Pakora, whisk besan, yogurt, turmeric, salt and water until smooth; rest 10 minutes.
Mix besan with onion slices and a little water to make pakora batter; fry spoonfuls at 175°C until golden and cooked through.
Bring yogurt mixture to a boil over medium, whisking continuously to prevent splitting.
Lower heat and simmer 25–30 minutes, stirring often, until kadhi thickens and raw besan smell disappears.
Add pakoras for the last 8 minutes so they soften but retain shape.
Temper cumin, mustard, dried chilli and curry leaves in oil and pour over.
Serve hot with rice.

name: Dhokla
title: Dhokla
description: Dhokla, a much-loved West Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Dhokla, whisk besan, yogurt, water, turmeric, lemon, sugar and salt to a smooth pourable batter; rest 10 minutes.
Grease a shallow steel tray and bring water to a boil in the steamer.
Fold fruit salt into batter only when the steamer is ready; pour immediately into the tray.
Steam over boiling water 15 minutes without opening the lid; a skewer should come out clean.
Cool 5 minutes and cut into squares while still warm.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in oil, add a spoon of water and pour over the dhokla.
Garnish with coriander and serve with green chutney.

name: Thepla
title: Thepla
description: Thepla, a much-loved West Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Thepla, wash methi, drain and chop finely; mix with atta, yogurt, turmeric, chilli, sesame, oil and salt.
Add water gradually and knead a soft dough; cover and rest 15 minutes.
Divide and roll each ball thinly to about 15 cm.
Heat tawa on medium; cook until small bubbles appear, flip and brush lightly with oil.
Flip again and press until golden spots form on both sides and the methi dough is cooked through.
Stack under a cloth to keep soft.
Serve with yogurt, pickle or as a travel snack.

name: Misal Pav
title: Misal Pav
description: Misal Pav, a much-loved West Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Misal Pav, soak moth beans overnight, drain and sprout 24–36 hours; pressure-cook sprouts until tender but intact.
Heat oil, crackle mustard and curry leaves, then sauté onion until golden.
Add tomatoes, turmeric and misal masala; cook until thick and oil separates.
Add sprouts with cooking liquid and simmer 12–15 minutes so they absorb the spicy gravy.
Adjust salt and hot water to make pourable tarri; add farsan only at serving.
Ladle misal into bowls and top with farsan, onion, coriander and lemon.
Serve with toasted pav while farsan remains crisp.

name: Vada Pav
title: Vada Pav
description: Vada Pav, a much-loved West Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Vada Pav, mash boiled potatoes; temper mustard in oil, add curry leaves, chilli and turmeric, then mix into potatoes with coriander and salt.
Cool and shape into 8 balls; chill 10 minutes so they hold together.
Whisk besan, salt and baking soda with water to a thick coating batter.
Heat oil to 175°C; dip each potato ball and fry, turning until evenly golden and crisp.
Drain on a rack and check the coating is cooked through at the seams.
Split pav, spread dry garlic chutney and place one hot vada inside.
Serve immediately with chutney and green chilli.

name: Litti Chokha
title: Litti Chokha
description: Litti Chokha, a much-loved East Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Litti Chokha, mix atta, salt and ghee with water into firm dough; cover and rest 20 minutes.
Combine sattu, mustard oil, pickle masala, ajwain and lemon with a little water; filling should hold but remain crumbly.
Divide dough, fill each ball generously and seal without cracks.
Roast over charcoal or bake at 200°C, turning every 8 minutes, until browned and cooked through, about 25–30 minutes.
Roast eggplant and tomatoes until charred and soft; peel and mash with onion, chilli, mustard oil and salt.
Crack a litti to check the centre is not doughy; brush with ghee.
Serve litti with chokha.

name: Dal Baati Churma
title: Dal Baati Churma
description: Dal Baati Churma, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Dal Baati Churma, rinse toor and chana dal; pressure-cook with turmeric until soft, then whisk lightly.
Knead atta, semolina, salt and ghee with little water into a stiff dough; rest 15 minutes.
Shape baati, score the top and bake at 190°C for 30–35 minutes, turning halfway.
Temper cumin in ghee, add tomato and garam masala, stir into dal and simmer 5 minutes.
Crush one baati to check the centre is cooked; bake longer if dense.
Crush a baati while warm and mix with powdered jaggery and ghee for churma.
Dip baati in ghee and serve with dal and churma.

name: Fish Fry
title: Fish Fry
description: Fish Fry, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Fish Fry, pat fish steaks completely dry and score shallow cuts so marinade reaches the centre.
Rub ginger-garlic, chilli, turmeric, lemon and salt over both sides; rest 20 minutes.
Coat lightly with rice flour and semolina immediately before frying.
Heat oil over medium; shallow-fry 4–5 minutes per side, depending on thickness.
Turn once when edges turn opaque and crust releases; the centre should flake but remain moist.
Drain on a rack so steam does not soften the crust.
Serve hot with onion and lemon.

name: Chicken 65
title: Chicken 65
description: Chicken 65, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Chicken 65, cut chicken into even bite-size pieces; mix with yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli, turmeric, flours and salt and marinate 30 minutes.
Heat oil to about 170°C and fry in small batches so the temperature does not drop.
Turn until crisp and deep red-gold, about 5–6 minutes; check one thick piece is cooked through and drain.
In a clean pan, heat a teaspoon of oil and crackle mustard; add curry leaves and slit chillies.
Return chicken and toss 30 seconds to coat without softening its crust.
Squeeze lemon over and adjust salt while hot.
Serve immediately as a starter.

name: Tandoori Chicken
title: Tandoori Chicken
description: Tandoori Chicken, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Tandoori Chicken, score chicken legs to the bone in 2–3 places so marinade can reach the meat.
Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli, turmeric, garam masala, lemon, mustard oil and salt; rub into every cut and marinate at least 4 hours.
Heat oven to 220°C or prepare a hot grill; set chicken on a rack over a tray.
Roast 25–35 minutes, turning once and basting, until the edges char lightly.
Check the thickest part reaches 74°C and juices run clear; rest 5 minutes.
For stronger char, broil 2–3 minutes while watching continuously.
Serve with sliced onion and lemon.

name: Hyderabadi Biryani
title: Hyderabadi Biryani
description: Hyderabadi Biryani, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Hyderabadi Biryani, rinse basmati until clear and soak 20 minutes; marinate chicken in yogurt, ginger-garlic, biryani masala, chilli, turmeric, lemon and salt for 30 minutes.
Fry sliced onion in ghee until deep golden and reserve half; add marinated chicken and cook until the outside is sealed.
Boil rice in salted water with cardamom, bay leaf and cloves until 70% cooked; a grain should break with a firm white centre. Drain immediately.
Layer half the rice over chicken; scatter mint, coriander and fried onion, add remaining rice and drizzle ghee.
Seal the pot tightly and cook on a tawa over low flame 25–35 minutes; do not lift the lid during dum.
Rest sealed 10 minutes; chicken must reach 74°C at the thickest piece and rice should be tender, not mushy.
Lift from the side to preserve layers and serve with raita.

name: Dalia Upma
title: Dalia Upma
description: Dalia Upma, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Dalia Upma, measure rava or broken wheat and finely chop onion, chilli, ginger and vegetables.
Dry-roast rava over low heat 4–5 minutes until aromatic; for dalia, toast 3 minutes then rinse.
Heat oil or ghee, crackle mustard and urad dal, then sauté curry leaves, chilli, ginger and onion 3 minutes.
Add diced vegetables, turmeric and salt and cook 3 minutes until they begin to soften.
Pour in boiling water carefully, then rain in the grain while stirring to avoid lumps.
Cover on low 5–8 minutes until tender with no water pooling; fluff with a fork.
Finish with coriander and lemon and serve hot.

name: Pesarattu
title: Pesarattu
description: Pesarattu, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Pesarattu, soak whole green moong and rice in plenty of water for 4 hours; drain and rinse.
Grind with ginger, green chilli, cumin, salt and enough water to make a smooth pourable batter; rest 15 minutes.
Heat a seasoned tawa over medium-high; wipe with a little oil and test with a few drops of water—they should sizzle away.
Pour a ladle of batter and spread in outward circles; scatter chopped onion over Pesarattu or Onion Uttapam and press lightly.
Drizzle oil around the edge and cook 2–3 minutes until golden and releasing easily; flip briefly if you want both sides browned.
Fold the dosa while hot; reduce heat if the underside darkens before the centre sets.
Serve immediately with ginger or coconut chutney.

name: Macher Jhol
title: Macher Jhol
description: Macher Jhol, a much-loved East Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Macher Jhol, pat rohu or catla steaks dry and rub with turmeric and salt; rest 10 minutes.
Heat mustard oil until shimmering; shallow-fry fish 2 minutes per side until lightly golden, then lift out.
In the same oil, add cumin and chilli; fry potato wedges until their edges turn golden.
Add grated ginger, tomato and water; simmer until potatoes are nearly tender, about 8 minutes.
Return fish and simmer gently 6–8 minutes without stirring hard; the flesh should flake at the thickest point.
Taste the thin jhol for salt and chilli; add hot water if it has reduced too much.
Finish with coriander and serve with steamed rice.

name: Goan Prawn Curry
title: Goan Prawn Curry
description: Goan Prawn Curry, a much-loved West Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Goan Prawn Curry, toast coriander seeds and dried chillies briefly until fragrant; cool, then grind with grated coconut, turmeric, tamarind and a little water to a smooth masala.
Rinse prawns and pat dry; slice onion and measure coconut milk.
Heat coconut oil and sauté onion until soft, not browned.
Add ground coconut masala and cook on low 5 minutes, stirring, until aromatic.
Stir in coconut milk and 1/2 cup water; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add prawns and cook only 3–4 minutes until opaque and curled; overcooking makes them tough.
Taste for salt and tang; serve at once with rice.

name: Khandvi
title: Khandvi
description: Khandvi, a much-loved West Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Khandvi, whisk besan, yogurt, water, turmeric, ginger-chilli paste and salt until completely smooth.
Spread a teaspoon of batter thinly on a steel plate; keep plates ready before cooking because the mixture sets quickly.
Cook the batter in a heavy pan over medium-low, stirring continuously 8–10 minutes until thick and glossy.
Spread a thin layer over the plates immediately; when cool enough to touch, cut strips and roll tightly.
Temper mustard and sesame in oil; add curry leaves and pour over the rolls.
Check rolls hold their shape and are soft inside, not sticky or raw.
Garnish with coconut and serve at room temperature.

name: Patishapta
title: Patishapta
description: Patishapta, a much-loved East Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Patishapta, cook coconut and jaggery on low until sticky and dry enough to hold; add cardamom and cool.
Whisk rice flour, maida and milk into a thin lump-free crepe batter; rest 20 minutes.
Heat a lightly greased tawa on medium-low and pour a thin oval of batter.
When the top loses its wet sheen but the underside remains pale, place coconut filling down the centre.
Roll the crepe around the filling and cook seam-side down 30 seconds to seal.
Repeat, greasing the tawa lightly between crepes.
Serve warm as a Bengali winter sweet.

name: Mango Lassi
title: Mango Lassi
description: Mango Lassi, a much-loved North Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Mango Lassi, chill mango pulp, yogurt and milk for 30 minutes so the lassi is refreshing.
Add mango, yogurt, milk, sugar, cardamom and ice to a blender.
Blend 30–45 seconds until smooth and lightly frothy.
Taste; add sugar if mango is tart or milk if too thick.
Pour into chilled glasses.
Garnish with cardamom or chopped pistachios if available.
Serve immediately; never heat the yogurt.

name: Bisi Bele Bath
title: Bisi Bele Bath
description: Bisi Bele Bath, a much-loved South Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Bisi Bele Bath, rinse rice and toor dal separately; pressure-cook with turmeric and water until very soft.
Simmer diced vegetables in water until just tender; keep the cooking liquid.
Dissolve tamarind pulp and bisi bele bath powder in the vegetable liquid and boil 5 minutes to remove raw sourness.
Add cooked rice, dal and vegetables to the spiced broth; stir over low heat until creamy and cohesive.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in ghee; fry peanuts until crisp and pour over.
Adjust salt and thickness with hot water; the bath should be soft, not dry or soupy.
Serve hot with extra ghee and papad.

name: Kosha Mangsho
title: Kosha Mangsho
description: Kosha Mangsho, a much-loved East Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Kosha Mangsho, rinse and pat the mutton dry; coat with yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli, turmeric and salt and rest 30 minutes.
For Kosha Mangsho, brown onion slowly in a heavy pot; cook deeper for a dark kosha-style gravy.
Add the listed spices and tomato and sauté 8 minutes until thick and oil separates.
Add marinated meat and turn each piece in masala until no raw surfaces remain.
Add measured water, cover and simmer low for 60–75 minutes; stir every 10 minutes so the base does not catch.
Check chicken reaches 74°C or mutton yields easily to a fork; reduce uncovered if gravy is thin.
Finish with coriander or curry leaves and serve hot with rice or roti.

name: Undhiyu
title: Undhiyu
description: Undhiyu, a much-loved West Indian Indian preparation made with traditional spices and household ingredients.
instructions: For Undhiyu, cut potatoes, yam, eggplant and beans into large even pieces; slit small eggplants without cutting through.
Mix coconut, coriander, ginger, garlic, chilli, sesame and salt into coarse masala and stuff the eggplants.
Heat oil and layer firm vegetables first, then softer vegetables and stuffed eggplants.
Sprinkle remaining masala and water; cover and cook low 25–30 minutes, shaking the pot gently rather than stirring.
Check vegetables with a knife; they should be tender yet hold shape and the masala cling.
Fold in methi muthia during the final 10 minutes if using.
Finish with lemon and coriander; serve with puri or rotli.

name: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad Bowl
title: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad Bowl
description: A refreshing quinoa bowl with chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, herbs and lemon dressing.
instructions: Rinse quinoa under cold water until it no longer foams; drain well.
Simmer quinoa in 1 cup water with a pinch of salt 15 minutes until the germ unfurls and water is absorbed.
Rest covered 5 minutes, fluff and cool slightly so it does not wilt vegetables.
Dice cucumber and onion, halve tomatoes and drain chickpeas thoroughly.
Whisk lemon juice, olive oil and salt, then toss through chickpeas and vegetables.
Fold in quinoa and parsley gently; taste and add lemon or salt as needed.
Serve at room temperature or chilled.

name: Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
title: Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
description: Individual chocolate cakes with a soft, flowing chocolate centre.
instructions: Heat oven to 220°C; butter two ramekins and dust the insides with cocoa powder.
Melt dark chocolate and butter over barely simmering water; stir smooth and cool 2 minutes.
Whisk egg, yolk and sugar until pale, then fold in chocolate, flour and salt.
Divide batter between ramekins and set on a tray; avoid overfilling so the centres stay molten.
Bake 10–12 minutes until edges are set but centres wobble when nudged.
Rest 1 minute, loosen edges and invert onto warm plates.
Serve immediately while the centre flows.
